title: Load Balancers: Where TLS Should Terminate

scenes.say: If you're running secure apps, where should you actually terminate TLS? At the load balancer, or all the way at the backend?

scenes.label: VIP
scenes.sub: The virtual IP is where clients connect first.
scenes.say: The VIP, or virtual IP, is the address clients hit. It's the front door to your app.

rows.b: LB decrypts, backends get plain HTTP

scenes.say: You can end TLS at the load balancer, so it decrypts traffic and sends plain HTTP to backends. Or, keep TLS end-to-end, so the LB just passes encrypted traffic through.
Ending TLS at the load balancer means one spot to manage certificates, and your WAF can see the traffic. But, backend traffic isn't encrypted, which can be a problem for compliance.

scenes.question: TLS should always end at the backend?
scenes.right: Usually, TLS ends at the LB. Only go end-to-end if compliance or policy requires it.
scenes.say: A common trap: Should TLS always end at the backend for security? Usually, it's best at the load balancer—unless compliance says otherwise.
